topic: Thread Scheduling: Cache Coldness and Pollution Penalty
explanation: A significant penalty of context switching occurs when the scheduler moves a software thread to a different core than it previously ran on. (1) The CPU caches on the new core are 'cold,' meaning they contain little data useful to the newly scheduled thread, forcing slower memory access. (2) Running the new thread 'pollutes' the cache of the new core by displacing data useful to the threads previously scheduled there, negatively impacting those threads when they are eventually rescheduled.
practical_example: A data processing pipeline relies heavily on cache locality for speed. Due to oversubscription, the OS frequently migrates the worker threads between cores. This migration causes continuous cache misses and pollution, resulting in the pipeline running significantly slower than if the threads were pinned to specific cores.
